note: Vol. I No. 51. The town is on page 3 column 2 — which is the richest single column of the month: the committee of twenty, two marriages, an obituary out of Fort Dearborn, a dancing school and the marine list all stand in it — and on page 4, where the standing advertisements run. No letter list of any post office stands in this issue. AMENDED 2026-08-29 by T-0350: c012 added — the SECOND of seven printings of D. Weaver's notice of a building on Lot 2, block 1, North Water street, on page 3 column 3, cut with `locator.spans` out of an alternating pair of physical columns.

Eighteen names survive legibly out of what the running head calls a committee of twenty; the nineteenth is cut to a fragment before 'S. Clybourn' and is not guessed at. This is the single densest roster of corroborated residents in the month — not letter-list names but men the paper puts in a room on a dated evening — and it names the Exchange Coffee House for the second time in three weeks, after the trustees met there on 3 November. Two readings are supplied and marked: 'Doct. E. S.' with the surname cut is read as Kimberly, the physician of that name in the town, and 'M. S. Han:' is left with a query. The paragraph above the roster is the call to meet; the two are quoted together because the segmenter interleaves them.

Both names are recorded as the paper spells them, with the OCR's own confusions bracketed; no identity merge is proposed for either, and neither is claimed to be documented anywhere else in this corpus. claims.notes: A DEATH INSIDE FORT DEARBORN, A BURIAL BY THE GARRISON AND THE CITIZENS TOGETHER, AND A FUNERAL SERMON APPOINTED AT THE METHODIST CHAPEL. The chapel is the claim's value to the model: the town has a Methodist meeting house in November 1834 that is distinct from the Presbyterian church used for the temperance and library meetings, and the paper names both within the month. Mrs. Baxley's memoir, read at her funeral by the pastor of the Methodist Episcopal Church, is printed in the next issue (1834-11-26 page 2), which corroborates both the chapel and her name. Her father's surname is cut at the column edge and is left unsupplied; the age is read as the 32d year.

claims.normalized: [F]or Sale or To Let, [THE] building on Lot 2, in bl[ock 1, on North Wa]ter street. Apply [to D. WEAVER.] [Chicag]o, No[v]. 12, 18[uncertain: 84 / 34].—50 — after “Apply” the line carries “ae 1, e8 Norte”, a second damaged impression of “ock 1, on North” that the segmenter has folded into the same line; it stands in the quote and is not read as new matter.
claims.notes:
THE SECOND PRINTING OF D. WEAVER'S STANDING NOTICE, AND THE SECOND OF THE TWO T-0328 DID NOT HAVE. Page 3 column 3 here is one of the alternating pairs: each line carries this column on the left and another advertisement's on the right, so the claim is cut with `locator.spans` (T-0261) rather than quoting whole lines — line 2578 whole would say “or Sale or To Let, : _Ottarea, Ml.”, and the tail of it belongs to somebody else.

NO ENTITY IS RECORDED, BECAUSE THIS SETTING NAMES NOBODY. The line that should carry “Apply to D. WEAVER.” loses the name to the weave. The notice is identified as Weaver's on its own body text and its key, not on a name read in from another issue: “For Sale or To Let,” over “building on Lot 2, in bl[ock 1] … [North Wa]ter street. Apply”, under the dateline “Nov. 12, 1834.—50” — the same words, the same lot, the same street and the same insertion key as the six other printings. Identification `inferred` on that match; a person minted from another column's setting would be a person this column never named, which is the discipline 1834-12-10 c011 states.

IT IS ALSO A WITNESS ON THE LOT NUMBER, and it reads 2 in a body line whose only damage is the cut at the column edge. That makes five settings reading Lot 2 against 1834-12-17's one reading 9, with 1834-11-12 printing no digit. T-0328's reading is strengthened, not changed, and is not reopened here.

THE COPY DATE IS 12 NOVEMBER 1834, DECIDED BY T-0350 OVER SEVEN PRINTINGS AND BY THE PAPER'S OWN INSERTION KEY. The advertisement ran SEVEN times, not five: it opens in Vol. I No. 50 of 1834-11-12 (c015) and No. 51 of 1834-11-19 (c012), two settings T-0328's tally did not have because neither is findable by the advertiser's name — 1834-11-12 sets it “D. WEAVE.R” and the surviving span of 1834-11-19 prints no name at all. They were found by searching the run for the notice's own body text instead. The datelines across the seven: Nov. 12 at 1834-11-12, 1834-11-19, 1834-11-26 and 1834-12-03; Nov. 13 at 1834-12-17; Nov. 19 at 1834-12-24; and no legible day or month at 1834-12-10. Four to one to one.

AND THE TALLY IS NOT WHAT DECIDES IT — THE ADVERTISEMENT'S OWN KEY DOES. Every legible setting tails its dateline with the figure 50: “1834.—50” at 1834-11-19 and “1881-50” at 1834-11-26, “1831. SO” at 1834-12-03, “1631.—00” at 1834-12-10, “1834-SD” at 1834-12-24 and “1831 -5)” at 1834-11-12. In this paper that trailing figure is not part of the date: it is THE NUMBER OF THE ISSUE THE COPY IS KEYED TO, the first number published on or after the dateline. It is checkable on other advertisers in the same columns — J. Bates's blacksmith-tools notice sets “Nov. 5, 1834.—49” and Vol. I No. 49 was published on 5 November; a For Sale notice sets “Nov. 26, 1834-52” against No. 52 of 26 November; two December notices set “Dec. 16, 1834.-3” and “Dec. 11, 1834.-3” against Vol. II No. 3, the first number published after either date. Vol. I No. 50 was published on 12 NOVEMBER 1834, so a key of 50 admits only a dateline falling after 5 November and on or before 12 November. Nov. 13 and Nov. 19 both fall outside it and would key 51; Nov. 12 is the only one of the three readings the key allows, and it is the reading four of the seven settings print.

THE KEY IS A FUNCTION OF THE DATELINE, NOT A CLAIM ABOUT FIRST APPEARANCE, and that distinction is kept because one of the four control notices breaks the looser version: Bates's “Nov. 5, 1834.—49” does not itself stand in No. 49 of 5 November, but first appears in No. 50. The key records the week the copy was handed in. For this notice the two coincide anyway — it is absent from No. 49 of 1834-11-05 and from No. 48 of 1834-10-29 (checked; the “For Sale or Rent” standing in both is G. Blanshard's, a different notice), and it first stands in No. 50.

THE TICKET'S DOUBT IS ANSWERED RATHER THAN OVERRIDDEN. T-0350 weighed 12 against 19 partly on the ground that Nov. 12 would be a fortnight before the notice's first appearance where Nov. 19 would be a week. Both halves rested on 1834-11-26 being the first appearance; it is the third. Dated 12 November the notice is dated the day it first ran, which is the same-day pattern “Nov. 5, 1834.—49” and “Nov. 26, 1834-52” show.

NOTHING IS AMENDED TO AGREE WITH ANYTHING. Every printing keeps its own verbatim dateline, including the two that read 13 and 19, and each claim's `ad_copy_date.verbatim` is that setting's own text. The dossier is docs/RESEARCH/weaver_building_north_water_block_1.md.
